title: reduction of foreigners in Brasileirão sparks debate among clubs
seoTitle: Reduction of Foreign Players in Brasileirão Sparks Debate
subtitle: the new rule could clear the way for homegrown talent
excerpt: The CBF has approved reducing the limit of foreign players in the Brasileirão from nine to five, in stages until 2030.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On Monday, the CBF approved the gradual reduction of the maximum limit of foreign players in the Brasileirão, dropping from nine to five players per match, in stages until 2030. The decision was made by Série A and B clubs, with the exception of Flamengo and Bahia, who voted against it.

clubs supporting the measure

Palmeiras, Corinthians, and Santos showed support for the reduction, arguing that the measure could stimulate investment in athlete development. The São Paulo club relies on its youth academy work and believes the rule will allow it to uncover even more youngsters.

divergent opinions

Flamengo and Bahia voted against the new rule. The Rubro-Negro argued that the world's top leagues do not have foreign player limits and that the presence of foreign players contributes to the high level of the championship. The club also highlighted that many Brazilian talents play abroad.

impact on clubs with an excess of foreigners

Five elite clubs, among them Athletico, Botafogo, Vasco, Flamengo, and Grêmio, have already exceeded the current limit of nine foreigners. They will need to reduce the number of players of other nationalities on their rosters to comply with the new rule.

international expert views

Dejan Petkovic, former player and commentator, criticized the change, stating that it will not solve player development in Brazil. He pointed out that the quest for results can harm the development of youth and questioned the classification of South Americans as foreigners. Meanwhile, Italian coach Carlo Ancelotti supported the measure, stating that reducing the number of foreigners can open opportunities for talents formed in national youth systems.

gradual rollout of the rule until 2030

The CBF established that, starting next season, the limit will be eight foreigners, dropping to seven in 2028, six in 2029, and finally five in 2030. The measure aims to curb the increase of foreign players in the Brasileirão in recent years.

With information from UOL, Estadão, VEJA.
